featured_image.name: Netanyahu says campaign against Iran 'not over,' admits ...

items.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu declared Saturday night that Israel's campaign against Iran "is not over," issuing a video statement that touted what he called "historic achievements" while acknowledging that "we still have more to do," even as U.S. and Iranian negotiators held their first round of ceasefire talks in Islamabad.[1][2]

items.title: Artemis II crew gets hero's welcome in Houston
items.description: The four astronauts of NASA's Artemis II mission arrived at Ellington Field near Johnson Space Center on Saturday to a thunderous welcome, reuniting with their families for the first time since completing a record-breaking 10-day voyage around the Moon. The crew was greeted with cheers, a standing ovation, and embraces from NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman.[1][2]

items.title: U.S.-Iran peace talks begin in Pakistan as Wall Street posts best week since November

featured_image.name: Stock market news for April 8, 2026 - CNBC

items.description: U.S. stocks posted their strongest weekly gains in months as a fragile ceasefire between Washington and Tehran eased fears of a wider conflict and sent oil prices tumbling. The S&P 500 finished the week ending April 10 up roughly 3.6%, its best performance since November, while the Nasdaq Composite surged about 4.7% and the Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 3.6%, returning to positive territory for the year.[1][2][3]

items.title: Altman ties Molotov cocktail attack to New Yorker expose

featured_image.name: Founder Sam Altman Back as OpenAI CEO Under Revamped Board

items.description:
Hours after a 20-year-old man threw a Molotov cocktail at his San Francisco home early Friday morning, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman published a lengthy personal blog post responding to a sweeping New Yorker investigation into his character and leadership — drawing a direct line between the article's rhetoric and the attack on his family.

"There was an incendiary article about me a few days ago," Altman wrote in the post, published April 10. "Now I am awake in the middle of the night and pissed, and thinking that I have underestimated the power of words and narratives."[1]

items.title: GOP lawmakers accuse EU of election meddling in Hungary

featured_image.name: EU Commission presses Hungary to clarify Russia spying allegations

items.description: Two Republican members of Congress sent a letter to European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen on Thursday accusing the EU of "unprecedented, undemocratic interference" in Hungary's parliamentary elections, adding a new dimension to a transatlantic dispute over the vote set for Sunday, April 12.

items.title: US launches mine clearance mission in Strait of Hormuz

items.description: Two US Navy guided-missile destroyers transited the Strait of Hormuz on Saturday in the first such passage since the US-Iran conflict began six weeks ago, as US Central Command launched an operation to clear sea mines from one of the world's most critical oil shipping routes.

items.title: Flávio Bolsonaro edges past Lula for first time in Datafolha poll
items.description: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva finds himself numerically behind Senator Flávio Bolsonaro for the first time in a Datafolha poll, with the latest survey released Saturday showing the right-wing lawmaker at 46% to Lula's 45% in a simulated second-round runoff for the October presidential election. The one-point gap falls within the poll's two-percentage-point margin of error, making it a statistical tie — but the symbolic shift marks a new chapter in what has become one of Brazil's tightest presidential races in years.[1]

items.title: Head swelled to 'basketball size': How it feels to eject from a fighter jet
items.description: A retired F-15 pilot who survived one of the fastest known fighter jet ejections in history, describes what two US airmen would have faced when they did the same in Iran a week ago.

items.title: Russia accuses Ukraine of breaking Easter truce minutes after it began

featured_image.name: Russia and Ukraine agree to 32-hour Orthodox Easter ceasefire

items.description:
A Ukrainian drone struck a gas station in the town of Lgov in Russia's Kursk region on Saturday, injuring three people including a child, just minutes after a 32-hour Easter ceasefire announced by President Vladimir Putin took effect, according to regional governor Alexander Khinshtein. The attack, which Khinshtein reported via the messaging platform MAX, occurred shortly after the truce began at 4:00 p.m. Moscow time (1:00 p.m. GMT) on April 11.[1][2]

The incident immediately cast doubt over whether the rare pause in fighting — agreed to by both Moscow and Kyiv for Orthodox Easter — would hold, echoing a pattern from last year's Easter truce when each side accused the other of hundreds of violations.[3][4]

items.title: U.S. Navy ships cross Strait of Hormuz without Iran's approval

featured_image.name: If the US Navy can't open the Strait of Hormuz, it's mad to suggest ...

items.description: Several US Navy ships crossed the Strait of Hormuz on Saturday in a move that was not coordinated with Iranian forces, according to Axios reporter Barak Ravid, citing a US official. The transit marks the first time US naval vessels have passed through the strategic waterway without Iranian approval since the US-Iran conflict began on February 28, representing a direct challenge to Tehran's claim of control over the chokepoint.[1][2][3]
